const answers = [
["Q01","1) Start with 25 money. 2) Start with 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers on the reserve spaces. 3) Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4. 4) Draw 2 Final Scoring cards. 5) Put Animals side I in the leftmost slot (strength 1); put the other four side-I Action cards randomly in the remaining slots. 6) Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for the second, 2 for the third, and 3 for the fourth.","supported","Personal setup C1–F: 25 money; 1 active and 3 lying workers; draw 8/keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; Animals in leftmost slot; stagger appeal by turn order."],
["Q02","1) Setup places 4 face-up Base Conservation Projects in a four-player game and 3 in games with fewer players. 2) In a two-player game only, block the left level of the left project, the middle level of the middle project, the right level of the right project, and the three donation spaces in the left column; neither player may use those spaces. 3) In three- and four-player games no project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup. 4) Reveal the initial 6-card display after all players have chosen their starting hands.","supported","Setup 5b–5c and personal setup G."],
["Q03","1) After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one space right, and place the used card in slot 1. 2) Set strength, including any X-token boosts, before the action; each X-token adds +1 strength and returns to supply. Tokens gained during that action cannot boost it. 3) You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4) Resolve an “after finishing” effect after completing the action and moving the Action cards.","supported","Turn Structure: taking a turn, X-tokens and after-finishing effects."],
["Q04","1) No: you may not do nothing, and playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal regular action. 2) Instead, you may choose the alternative X-token action: select any Action card, take exactly 1 X-token, move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards as usual; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3) You cannot take this action if you already hold 5 X-tokens.","supported","Turn Structure and X-token action."],
["Q05","1) Once the Break token reaches the last space, ignore extra movement beyond that space. 2) The player who reaches it gains 1 X-token. 3) Finish the current turn; the break then occurs for everyone. 4) After the break, play continues clockwise with the next player.","supported","The Break track; Break procedure step 6."],
["Q06","1) Cards I: first advance the Break token 2 spaces, then either draw from the deck according to the strength table (maximum 3 draws, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card of choice regardless of reputation and do not draw from the deck. 2) Cards II: also advance 2 spaces; draw from the deck and/or display cards within reputation range in any order using the upgraded table. A snap is exactly 1 display card, works from strength 3, and ignores reputation; snapping has no deck draw. 3) Display cards taken during a turn are not replenished until the turn ends. 4) Hand limit is not enforced during the action; discard to the limit only at breaks.","supported","Cards action and Special Rules: Display timing and Hand size."],
["Q07","1) Reputation range includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. 2) Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3) At reputation 15, further reputation gains leave the counter at 15 and give 1 appeal per excess reputation step. 4) You may not look through the discard pile during the game.","supported","Reputation track and display."],
["Q08","1) Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different building types with total size no greater than strength, but never 2 identical buildings in one action. 2) Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3) The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4) Build only on empty map spaces; no extending off-map, overlap, water or rock. Spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. 5) Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. 6) Each pavilion immediately and once increases appeal by 1.","supported","Build action and placement rules."],
["Q09","1) Build I allows standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo (size 3). 2) Build II additionally allows Reptile Houses and Large Bird Aviaries (size 5 each), as well as restricted-icon map spaces. 3) The supply contains 4 tiles of each special-enclosure type; each zoo may have at most 1 of each type. 4) Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 5) Covering all map spaces except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.","supported","Buildings available through Build; full zoo map."],
["Q10","1) Bonuses gained earlier in an action may be used in later steps of that same action, but pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Thus previously gained money may pay for a later building, animal, or Association task if applicable. 2) Ordinary effects resolve immediately unless they say “after finishing”; after-finishing effects wait until the action is completed, including Action-card movement. 3) For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses their order.","supported","Turn Structure: X-tokens; animal effect timing; multiple simultaneous effects."],
["Q11","1) To play an animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, then provide legal housing and terrain adjacency; place its card by the map and resolve appeal and other effects. 2) A partner zoo on the animal’s continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon printed on that animal, so double matching icons reduce it by 6. 3) A standard enclosure must be empty, at least the animal’s printed minimum size, and is flipped as a whole to its occupied side; it normally houses one animal. 4) Petting Zoo animals must use a Petting Zoo; eligible reptiles and some birds may use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if their indicated token-space requirement fits, placing one supply player token per space used. Special enclosures are never flipped. 5) Meet water/rock adjacency for the chosen housing, including special enclosures; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not edges. 6) For multiple animals, finish each animal’s steps and immediate effects before the next; after-finishing effects wait until all animals are done and the Action card has moved.","supported","Animals action and enclosure-state table."],
["Q12","1) Animals II lets you play animals from display folders within your reputation range, with an extra cost equal to the folder number; hand and display animals may be mixed. 2) At strength 5+, you may optionally gain 1 reputation at the very start, before choosing animals, so the expanded range applies. 3) Do not replenish the display until the turn ends. 4) Animals II also permits animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.","supported","Animals action, Side II."],
["Q13","1) Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit; choose separately for each animal. 2) Each moved animal must be suitable for that enclosure, meet its water/rock adjacency, and fit remaining capacity. Add the number of supply player tokens shown for that animal to the new special enclosure; never flip the special enclosure. 3) For each relocated animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all that animal’s requirements, including terrain. If none meets all, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip none.","supported","Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure."],
["Q14","1) Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2; gain partner zoo 3; gain university 4; conservation project work 5. 2) Association I performs exactly 1 task and needs at least 1 active worker; action strength must meet the task strength. 3) If you already have 1 of your workers on that task, place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot perform it again until after the break. 4) Opponents’ workers on a task do not matter. 5) Association II can perform one or more different tasks, spending 1 or 2 of your workers per task, provided total task value is no greater than action strength.","supported","Association action: side I and side II."],
["Q15","1) Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty matching space on your zoo map; resolve a covered-space bonus immediately. 2) You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents, with a maximum of 4. 3) A third or fourth partner zoo requires Association II. A partner zoo grants its continent icon and reduces matching animal costs by 3 per matching continent icon. 4) Universities grant printed reputation and research icons; only the hand-limit university raises the hand limit from 3 to 5. When acquiring a university, take its reputation award and any covered-space bonus immediately.","supported","Association tasks; University tiles; Your zoo map."],
["Q16","1) Association project work may support a project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. With Association II the new card may instead come from the in-range display, paying its folder number; do not refill until turn end. 2) A newly played project goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards right; if this exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project. 3) Return tokens on a discarded project to their owners’ supplies, not to their map; previously activated map bonuses stay activated. 4) For support, meet a printed condition and choose a reward level with no player token on it; each project may normally be supported only once by you. Put a token from the left edge of your zoo map on the chosen condition, gain the project reward, and take the uncovered map bonus immediately, before or after the project reward. Recurring uncovered bonuses pay again each break.","supported","Association action: Conservation project work and overflow."],
["Q17","1) Release size categories must match the animal’s printed standard-enclosure requirement by category: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. It is not the actual occupied tile or special-enclosure capacity. 2) Before gaining conservation, lose only that animal’s printed appeal, then discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. 3) If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure satisfying all requirements, or the smallest satisfying size alone if none meets all, or none if no occupied enclosure meets size.","supported","Release into the wild projects."],
["Q18","1) Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand, requiring action strength at least its level and all left-side conditions; alternatively advance the Break token by strength and take that much money. 2) Sponsors II plays one or more cards from hand and/or the in-range display; for each display card pay its folder number and do not replenish until turn end. Sum of levels must be no more than action strength +1; meet conditions (and II permits upgrade-required conditions). 3) Resolve each card’s instant effects completely before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4) The money option on Sponsors II advances by strength and pays twice the strength in money, even if fewer steps remain before the last break space.","supported","Sponsors action."],
["Q19","1) Break order: discard to hand limit; return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock available partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2) Hand limit is normally 3 or 5 with the hand-limit university, checked only at breaks. 3) Each kiosk earns 1 money for every adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, but empty special enclosures do. 4) When several players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill the display after each such player’s income, before the next affected player chooses.","supported","Break procedure, steps 1–6."],
["Q20","1) At 2 conservation, choose either upgrade an Action card or activate an additional Association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus tile beside that space (if available); tiles are removed after use. At 10, the first player to reach it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2) End is checked at the end of your own turn or during a break, when Appeal and Conservation counters share a scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player’s turn waits until your own turn end or a break unless someone triggers end first. 3) If triggered at a turn end, the triggering player completes that turn and everyone else gets one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players get one more turn. 4) Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation. 5) VP equals your Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; tie goes to most supported conservation projects, then tied players share the win.","supported","Scoring / Victory Conditions."],
["Q21","1) Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place a random tile face up on each of the 4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 and two beside 8. Do not put tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons; return the other 5 tiles to the box. 2) Components are not forbidden by physical stock running out: use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.","supported","Global setup step 2; Component supply."],
["Q22","1) For advanced maps, take 2 random maps and choose 1, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose one each in reverse turn order; return unchosen maps. 2) Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built, with a kiosk tile placed over it as reminder. You may build adjacent to it.","supported","Personal setup A."],
["Q23","1) Seven player tokens start on the designated spaces at the left edge of each player’s zoo map; remaining tokens stay by the map. 2) Hire inactive workers from the lowest reserve space upward. 3) Some maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker; the summary does not specify which maps.","partial","Personal setup C2–C3; Special Rules: Association worker supply."],
["Q24","1) Flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II in its current slot. 2) The improved action is usable starting with your next action. 3) It counts as upgraded for conditions immediately, including during the action in which the upgrade was earned. 4) There are four upgrade sources, and one allows an alternative choice, so you cannot upgrade all five Action cards.","supported","Upgrading Action cards."],
["Q25","1) Cards I draw / discard at strengths 1–5 are: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. 2) A required discard may be a newly drawn card or one already in your hand.","supported","Cards draw tables."],
["Q28","1) Animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. 2) Bear and Petting Zoo animal count as categories unless explicitly excluded; bears may also carry herbivore or predator icons.","supported","Animal categories; Base glossary."],
["Q29","1) A donation requires Association II and at least 1 Association task performed in that same action; it needs no worker, and you may donate at most once per Association action. 2) Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area and cover it with a player token from your supply, gaining 1 conservation. Costs in order are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. 3) Once all but the last space are covered, each subsequent donation costs 12 money and places no further token.","supported","Association II donation rule."],
["Q30","1) Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, plus water/rock requirements in upper-left corners of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards; partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons also count. 2) Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons; university reputation and hand-limit benefits are not icons. 3) An effect can count its own card; doubled icons count twice, while distinct-icon-type requests count each type once. 4) Card text takes priority over general rules.","supported","Counting icons in your zoo; shared principles."],
["Q31","1) For a two-space water/rock requirement, count distinct adjacent terrain hexes: several touching edges to the same hex count as one, and a larger connected terrain region counts only the individual hexes actually adjacent. 2) Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.","supported","Shared principles: terrain adjacency."],
["Q32","1) Bringing a new Release into the Wild project into play grants 1 reputation; later support of an existing release project grants no reputation for that play bonus. 2) Breeding Program projects have the same condition for all three reward spaces; choose any available space under normal support rules.","supported","Release into the wild; Other illustrated project rewards."],
["Q33","1) In an “X : Y” effect, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. 2) A condition without a number, or with “per,” pays once per fulfillment. 3) A numbered threshold pays only once; if multiple thresholds are met, use the highest one met.","supported","Base glossary: shared principles."],
["Q34","1) Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. 2) Isolated means no adjacent covered space. 3) A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4) “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply; “any zoo” includes those for all players.","supported","Base glossary: shared principles."],
["Q35","1) Unique buildings must be placed when their Sponsor is played; they have no size-based construction payment. 2) Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip. Follow ordinary placement and printed terrain requirements. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and are not water or rock spaces. 3) If placement is impossible, the Sponsor card cannot be played.","supported","Unique buildings."],
["Q36","1) For a named Action ability, finish the Animals action and move its card to slot 1 before taking the granted action; use the named Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. 2) A named action cannot be replaced by the X-token action. 3) Determination grants any action and may choose the X-token alternative.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination."],
["Q37","1) Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds a chosen project to hand; Dominance gets its named project from that same deck. 2) Dominance does nothing if its named project is already in play. 3) Later, play and immediately support the obtained card through Association, placing it above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion / Dominance."],
["Q38","1) Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving that Action card. 2) Clever puts the chosen card in slot 1; Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or 5. 3) Moving to slot 1 shifts cards formerly to its left right. Moving to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Boost / Clever."],
["Q39","1) All affected zoos must have at least 5 appeal; the playing animal’s appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so normally need not count for target eligibility. 2) Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo meeting the threshold; Pilfering targets the highest-appeal zoo (and for Pilfering 2 separately the most-conservation zoo), each meeting it; Venom affects every other qualifying zoo with higher appeal than yours. 3) The group may use the cards’ alternative solo-marked text for interactive abilities without playing solo mode.","supported","Interactive abilities and eligibility."],
["Q40","1) Constriction 1 places one token on slot 5; Constriction 2 places tokens on slots 4 and 5. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 2) A constricted Action loses 2 strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action, and X-tokens may restore strength. 3) Return a used token after acting; unused tokens are cleared at the next break.","supported","Constriction clarification."],
["Q41","1) At effective strength zero or below, you may not use the constricted regular action as-is: spend enough X-tokens to reach at least strength 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 2) The X-token action is allowed only if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens.","supported","Constriction clarification; X-token action."],
["Q42","1) Digging 2 allows up to two selections among its two options, and you may choose again after each card. 2) If discarding a display card, replenish it immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2."],
["Q43","1) A flock animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo has a printed standard-enclosure requirement at least as large as the flock animal’s; that same host herbivore can host any number of flock animals. 2) Without a qualifying herbivore, house it normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 3) On release, no proof of the original housing is required: follow the release procedure to free an occupied enclosure even if the flock animal shared it; historical residents are not tracked.","supported","Flock Animal clarification."],
["Q44","1) Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2) Take a last-worker map reward if shown. 3) If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Full-throated."],
["Q45","1) Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards, adds one revealed Animal card to hand, and discards the rest. 2) If none is an Animal card, discard all revealed cards.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Hunter X."],
["Q46","1) Hypnosis chooses among tied highest-appeal players who have at least 5 appeal; if you are the target, it has no effect. 2) Copy only the target’s slot 1, 2 or 3, using that card’s owner’s upgraded/unupgraded side for the entire action. Other upgrade checks use your own cards. 3) You may spend your own X-tokens. Venom and Constriction on the copied card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. 4) Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally.","supported","Hypnosis clarification."],
["Q49","1) Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card. The next use executes that action twice in succession at the same base strength; move the card only after both executions. 2) Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3) After-finishing effects wait until both executions are complete. A break triggered during the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished. 4) Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; remove unused ones at the next break.","supported","Multiplier rules."],
["Q50","1) Each Multiplier adds one execution; two tokens permit up to three executions, not four. 2) Each execution may use different permitted choices. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but cannot mix an X-token action with a regular action.","supported","Multiplier rules."],
["Q51","1) Peacocking allows placing a Large Bird Aviary before Build II, provided your zoo does not already have an Aviary and there is a legal site. Build II is still required for restricted-icon map spaces. 2) Other placement restrictions remain. 3) Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing; place multiple buildings one at a time.","supported","Peacocking and Posturing clarifications."],
["Q52","1) Petting Zoo animals grant successive appeal of 3, 6 and 9. 2) The single Petting Zoo can hold at most 3 such animals. 3) They count as small animals.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Petting Zoo animal."],
["Q53","1) Pilfering 1 chooses a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; ties let you choose. If that would be you, it has no effect. 2) Pilfering 2 separately chooses the highest-appeal target and the most-conservation target, with each at least 5 appeal; ties can be chosen. A conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. 3) If all players have zero conservation, the conservation-target part has no effect; the highest-appeal part still resolves under the normal five-appeal and self-target rules. If one zoo qualifies for both, pilfer from it twice.","supported","Pilfering clarification."],
["Q54","1) The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2) With no hand cards, the target gives 5 money; with less than 5 money, the target gives a card. If the target has neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3) Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.","supported","Pilfering clarification."],
["Q55","1) Pouch tucks up to X hand cards under the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard its tucked cards but retain the appeal already gained. 2) Sunbathing lets you sell up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Pouch X and Sunbathing X."],
["Q56","1) A Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the player’s choices when they discard one card at that milestone. 2) At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card; each card is capped at 4 conservation points.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Resistance."],
["Q57","1) Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw the specified number randomly, make the card’s stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. 2) Scavenging 3 specifically draws 3 random cards, keeps 1 and discards the others.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Scavenging."],
["Q58","1) Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not draw from the deck as an alternative. 2) Sponsor Magnet finds a display Sponsor without a reputation-range restriction; if none is present, it has no effect. 3) Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Snapping / Sponsor Magnet."],
["Q59","1) Venom tokens go on cards in the lowest slots first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2) Using a marked card removes its Venom token and avoids all Venom fees that turn; this includes the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. 3) At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token and at least one remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; you cannot avoid payment by spending all your money. 4) Unused Venom tokens expire at the next break without effect.","supported","Venom clarification."],
["Q63","1) Veterinarian gives an immediate 2, 5 or 10 money for 1, 2 or 3 universities respectively. 2) It reduces the Association strength required for conservation project support from 5 to 4. 3) Its final reward is 1 conservation for having 3 universities.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 203 Veterinarian."],
["Q66","1) Medical Breakthrough’s immediate appeal is 2 per previously supported project, counted as the player tokens missing from the left edge of their zoo map. 2) It gives 1 conservation at each break.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 206 Medical Breakthrough."],
["Q67","1) Basic Research totals distinct continent and animal-category icon types together, excluding research; repeated or doubled copies of a type count once. 2) Gain 1 conservation per 2 types, rounding down. 3) Each other player gets 2 money per conservation point you gain.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 207 Basic Research."],
["Q68","1) Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon on play. 2) Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with 5 different animal categories.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 208 Science Library."],
["Q70","1) Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2) Each Americas icon played permits building one free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with at least 5 kiosks.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 210 Expert on the Americas."],
["Q72","1) Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2) For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card under this Sponsor for 2 appeal. 3) Tucked cards have no further function.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 212 Expert on Australia."],
["Q75","1) Each card places 2 supply tokens on itself. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly 1 token as any one icon; you cannot use both tokens on one support. 2) Projects originating as base cards but played above the board do not qualify. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with at least 5 project supports, counted by missing tokens on the map’s left edge.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 215 Global Breeding Program; 218 Breeding Program."],
["Q77","1) Engineer allows each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action, without extra strength. 2) Pay normal money and obey placement rules; special enclosures remain limited to one per type per zoo. Even if several different buildings are built, only one extra building is allowed. 3) Final scoring grants 5 appeal for a full map excluding water and rock.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 217 Engineer."],
["Q78","1) Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2) It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements for animals and unique buildings. 3) Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist or Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered for full-map scoring. 4) Final scoring gives 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum 3 pairs.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 219 Diversity Researcher."],
["Q80","1) Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers an extra choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on the border. 2) Several border bonuses give several extra choices, which may be identical or different. Resolve in any chosen order. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 221 Archaeologist."],
